extracted.intended_audience: Apple users and general tech-news readers (and product/AI teams interested in notification summarization)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for evaluating or producing short, push/notification-style summaries generated by on-device AI (Apple Intelligence) for news headlines; focuses on accuracy, trust, and operational constraints. Useful for product managers, newsroom partners, and policy reviewers assessing whether such summaries are fit for public consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy / factual correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Summaries sometimes get things quite wrong and misinform users (e.g., a summary claimed that Luke Littler had 'won PDC World Championship' when he had only completed a semi-final).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize factual correctness in brief summaries; incorrect statements about events or outcomes (wins vs. semi-finals, identity of people) are unacceptable. The BBC has complained these inaccuracies have appeared multiple times and urged Apple to fix this problem urgently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source fidelity / correct attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Condensing headlines must preserve the referent and meaning of the original story (example: a condensed claim 'Rafael Nadal comes out as gay' appears to have misattributed a story about Brazilian gay player Joao Lucas Reis da Silva to the Spanish Nadal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summaries should not change who or what a story is about; entity disambiguation and faithful preservation of the original headline's subject are required to avoid misleading readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hallucinations / do not invent facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must not create information on their own; Apple preloaded instructions such as 'Do not hallucinate. Do not make up factual information' into the system to counter hallucinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement and enforce explicit guardrails/prompting that instruct the model not to fabricate facts; monitor and test for hallucination modes especially in short-form outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve trust and brand integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Notifications bearing a publisher's name must not misrepresent that organisation's journalism — 'as the most trusted news media organisation in the world, it is crucial that audiences can trust any information or journalism published in our name and that includes notifications,' says the BBC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design summaries and notification flows to protect publisher trust and reputation; publishers should be able to ensure that automated summaries carrying their brand do not mislead audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity vs fidelity tradeoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Summaries are 'meant to save time for users' but condensation can cause loss or distortion of meaning leading to inaccurate notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When compressing headlines for notifications, balance conciseness with fidelity: do not sacrifice essential facts for brevity. Prefer slightly longer but accurate phrasing over misleading short reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model maturity and reliability for public information
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters Without Borders warned that 'generative AI services are still too immature to produce reliable information for the public.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the model is sufficiently robust for public-facing news summaries; err on the side of withholding automated summarization when reliability is not demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, auditability, and error correction under privacy constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixing accuracy is made harder because Apple 'does not actively monitor what users are seeing on devices' and prioritizes on-device processing for privacy, limiting visibility into outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide mechanisms to detect and correct erroneous summaries that respect user privacy (e.g., opt-in reporting, local logging with opt-in telemetry, automated on-device checks). Ensure there are audit trails or feedback channels so publishers and vendors can find and remedy systematic errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness and accountability from the vendor
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC and other groups expect Apple to acknowledge issues and fix them; Apple had yet to publicly comment on current complaints though Tim Cook previously acknowledged potential inaccuracies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vendors should publicly acknowledge problems, communicate remediation plans, and act quickly to address systemic errors in summaries used for news notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-deployment guardrails / prompt engineering
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple had preloaded instructions into the system to counter hallucinations (example phrases fed into the system when acting on prompts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before deploying summarization models, include hard guardrails, refusal behaviors, or constrained templates; use prompt engineering and system instructions that explicitly forbid fabricating facts and encourage safe defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and liability considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: There are calls (in comments and discourse) that companies should be held legally liable for misinformation produced under their brand — 'Apple should be held legally liable for this.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider legal risk and liability when deploying automated news summaries under third-party brands; include legal review, indemnities, and risk mitigation strategies (e.g., opt-ins, disclaimers, publisher controls).
